utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. There are no urgent preliminary matters. Therefore, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. I meanwhile use --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The situation which I described yesterday, the 15 bis, is still valid and therefore we'll sit again today with two Judges on the basis of the same considerations as I expressed yesterday. We can deal, perhaps, already briefly with a -- one matter. That is, that the map P02952, that the Chamber had asked the Prosecution to upload a version to better show the parts -- part of the map related to the testimony of Mr. Bukva. The Chamber understands that the Prosecution has uploaded into e-court this version of the map under Rule 65 ter 08282C and that the Prosecution intends to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That's accurate, Your Honour. Apparently there is also a brief translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- issue with respect to that and we'll get back to the Chamber on that issue as soon as we can consult with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll wait for that translation. Good morning, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just before I start, Mr. Lukic, and I suppose for the record I should say that I mean Mr. Mladic's counsel, and I have spoken about the associated exhibits. I will be using a number of them today. As Defence requests to tender those exhibits are pending, with the exception of two long assembly sessions from which we will agree on excerpts, we suggest jointly that they be assigned D numbers when they are used during the cross-examination if the Chamber is agreeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's understood and the Chamber agrees. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And with that, sir, yesterday at transcript page 25.410 you testified regarding UNPROFOR that: "We were in the same building, one room next to the other." During the time you were there, the 1st of July to the 19th of December 1992, you lived and worked in the PTT building; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You had your own offices where you slept.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that you received protests about shelling in Sarajevo from UNPROFOR personnel. Did you relay though protests to the Republika Srpska presidency as part of your reporting to them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not standard practice. There was lot of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you had no authority to investigate these matters. Did you pass them on to anyone with authority to investigate?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I had all authority. I did not require any piece of paper other than Mr. Karadzic's decision. For example, General Morillon asked that I give my consent for ten physicians to leave Sarajevo. I provided it to him, given the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there. There seems to be some confusion. Mr. Traldi did put it to you, and apparently on the basis of your testimony yesterday, that you had no authority to investigate any shelling incident that was reported to you. That is what the question is about. Could you please focus on his question that was that you received protests, whether you passed those on to anyone else where you had no authority to investigate it than yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the Prosecutor to bear in mind that I'm an engineer by profession. I know what the term "investigation" entails.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But your answer has shown that you are talking about different things. Therefore, I kindly ask you to answer that question, whether you passed on these protests which you had no authority to investigate yourself, whether you passed them on to anyone else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I refuse to accept the conclusion that it was an investigation. All protests received by both sides I forwarded to UNPROFOR orally and to the officials senior to me when I met with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you received protests from UNPROFOR or from the other side, did you relay them to more senior officials in the Bosnian Serb government?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many were received by them as well, and others I conveyed to those senior to me at the first opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And to whom senior to you did you convey them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this they were members -- I apologise. Members of the presidency, Biljana Plavsic, Mr. Koljevic, Mr. Karadzic at times, and so on and so forth. Sometimes messages were sent as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then you left Sarajevo when you became prime minister; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were based in Pale throughout 1993 and 1994; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm going to turn now to your time as prime minister. The prime minister had the legal responsibility to appoint a number of government officials; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can 65 ter 16715 be brought to the screen. These are the minutes of the 66th Session of the RS government dated the 20th of March 1993. And now that they're up, in fact, if we could please have item 45 on page 12 in English and 17 on the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you see there already, sir, in the middle of the page a reference to the appointment of members of your government's personnel commission; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see four names and then a representative of the SDS Main Board. Now, the four names we see include your vice-president and other members of -- other directors of ministry in your government; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two deputy prime ministers. I can't read the third name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Miroslav Toholj.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So two deputy prime ministers or deputy presidents and one minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Adzic was also a minister; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I didn't get that far on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So two deputy prime ministers, two ministers, and a representative of the SDS Main Board. The SDS is the only political party we see granted representation; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now can 65 ter 16716 be brought to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this will be a letter from the Executive Board of the SDS to you dated a couple of weeks later, the 12th of April 1993. So taking you first to item 2, we read: "In the National Assembly we have 7 out of 8 seats. Your Government has been voted for and elected by the Deputies of the Serbian Democratic Party. You ought to be the Government of the Serbian Democratic Party and you are the Executive Authority of the Assembly with the majority of seats of the Serbian Democratic Party, you implement the policy of that party."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 2 in both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And directing your attention to point 4, we read, specifically as to personnel: "As the party in power, we conduct the personnel policy, and without the Personnel Commission of the Party on all levels, from the municipality to the Republic, no appointments will be possible without our approval. The way that the Government used to appoint the managers of public companies and make other appointments without the approval of the Assembly, was the usurpation of the former Government." Now, do you see that text?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the former government referred to there is the Prime Minister's Djeric's government; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could 65 ter 07341 be brought to our screens. These are the minutes of the of 68th Session of the Republika Srpska government held about ten days later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the name of the former prime minister is not recorded properly. Can you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is Mr. Djeric's last name, is that D-j-e-r-i-c?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Djeric.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now as this comes up, if we could turn to item 36 on page 4 in the English and 13 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And here we read: "The discussion and the decision on the proposed personnel were adjourned. It was concluded that the Government Personnel Commission will hold consultations with the SDS organs, about the proposed candidates, and after that prepare the proposals for the Government." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So in these minutes your government is agreeing to consult with the SDS on appointments; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And without going into specific examples, that did happen, didn't it? The government did consult with the SDS in advance before appointing personnel in government positions as well as enterprise position, public companies?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, those needed to be agreed with President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As well as with representatives of the SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that 65 ter 16715 and 07341 be admitted as Defence exhibits because the request to tender them as associated exhibits is pending. I understand they've been tendered publicly and I don't see any reason that they need to be placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are these the full -- the full minutes or?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I believe so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we then have them marked for identification, then you could further consider, perhaps together with Mr. Ivetic, whether we need all of it. And there is always a possibility at a later stage to add portions of it so as to avoid that we have a lengthy, lengthy document which we would have to go through without the parties even knowing what may catch our eyes. Mr. Registrar, could you mark for identification --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the two numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 16715 will be MFI D629 [Realtime transcript read in error "D627"], and 65 ter number 07341 will MFI D630.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They are marked for identification. The Chamber is looking forward to a joint proposal what are the most relevant portions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it would be helpful if Mr. Registrar would repeat the 65 ter number. It's not recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 07341 will be MFI D630, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. I'm just thinking about 627 and then the next one, 630, but there may be an explanation for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd also tender as a Prosecution exhibit the other -- the letter I used which was not an associated exhibit and is very brief. That's 65 ter 16716.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar. That would be number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P6729, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think there is something wrong with the D627 number. It should be D629 because yesterday we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please look at page 9, line 4, where it reads that 65 ter 16715 will be MFI'd as D and then what number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI D629, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what caught my eye before. This being corrected, Mr. Traldi, you -- no, let me just see. One second, please. Yes, P6729 is admitted into evidence. You may proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Can 65 ter 02382 be brought to our screens. And this is the transcript of the 34th Session of the RS Assembly. And if we could have page 168 in the English and 178 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We had, I think, the correct page in the English -- or, I'm sorry, in the B/C/S a moment ago -- but we seem -- we may have lost it. I think that's the one now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So when we see you speaking at the top of the page in B/C/S and in the middle of the page in English, you say: "We have several objections that the propositions of certain municipalities, parties, and companies are being withheld for a long time. However, I can say that the government is not keeping any acts, but is sending them to the party ..." By "the party" you meant the SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "... from the moment the party started working and immediately after they come from the party, they are being sent to the first Government session to come. I really do not know why certain proposals did not pass through." Those are your words; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're explaining that there are delays in certain appointments because of delays in getting approval from the SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the case for the most part, but there were other reasons as well due to the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, a portion of this session is already P2508 and Mr. Lukic, Mr. Stojanovic, Mr. Ivetic, and I perhaps will all speak and agree on additional portions to be admitted. There are some others that are identified in the witness's statement as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means that we don't have to reserve a number at this moment, that at this moment there is nothing specifically to be done but that soon you'll upload a new version which relevant portions, both of previous testimonies, and now to be added new portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear and hereby on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn, briefly now, sir, to some events from early in your time as prime minister?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can we have, please, 65 ter 02538.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: These are the minutes of the 61st Session of the government dated 21st of December 1992. And as they come up, this was the session at which the duties of prime minister were handed over to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 19 of your statement, you say that at this session, you insisted that stolen property should be returned to its rightful owners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 4 in both the English and the B/C/S. And in the English, I'm looking at the third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And here we have your actual words, and you say that government bodies should consistently apply regulations regarding war booty and properties that were not attend in a legal way. And then you say: "All measures should be taken in order to return illegally obtained properties to their original owners, i.e., to government bodies, if ownership couldn't be proven." So if ownership couldn't be proven, illegally obtained property was to be provided to the government; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can the Prosecution please have 65 ter 16715. These are the minutes of the 66th Session of the RS Government. And I believe this has already been assigned a D number MFI 629, I think. Now if we could have page 3 in the English and 5 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the bottom, we'll see item 2 dealing with the financial status of the VRS. And at the end of the page in English, we see --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm not sure we have the right B/C/S text highlighted. Can we zoom back out? And we're looking for what would be "ad 2," so maybe -- so beginning at the bottom of this page. So beginning at the bottom of the page in both languages. And I apologise. But if we could turn to the next now in both languages and looked at subpoint 4. We'll need one more page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read: "Place all war booty, from material assets to money and foreign currency considered socially-owned property, under the control of the state. "Material assets and money seized from war profiteers and money earned in unlawful and illegal ways is to be placed under the control of the state and used for the defence of the Republic." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Dr. Lukic, these minutes reflect the efforts of your government to collect unlawfully obtained money and property and use it to finance the army; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the army. Most often refugees, many others, the wounded, the sick.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking what these minutes reflect. Not about your policy more generally. What these minutes reflect is using this unlawfully obtained funds for the defence of the republic; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it says "for the defence of the republic," it does not mean only the army. The army was not the only one that was defending the republic. The categories that I referred to were in a particularly difficult situation, so I am telling you what were all the things that were done and why these things were done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this discussion takes place in the context of an agenda item related to the financing of the VRS, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meaning the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I mean by VRS.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then could you please put a direct question to me to which I can give you a direct answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. My direct question is: This discussion of what to do with illegally obtained property that we see here in these minutes took place in the context of an agenda item at a government meeting about the financing of the VRS; didn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially of the army. But since I see that you're stepping around the army, I need to tell you the following: The Army of Republika Srpska was financed from all possible sources, and you need to know that we exported electricity to Serbia and Croatia and that we were compensated for that. We exported timber, coal, and we even sold -- or, actually, we maintained and repaired aircraft engines for British and some Arab clients, some Arab countries as well. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, that all may be true. The question of Mr. Traldi is whether this discussion was under the heading of financing problems in the Army of Republika Srpska. So apart from what other financial issues there may have been, but whether this discussion, he just referred to, whether that was part of an agenda item about financing problems of the army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the general problems of financing were discussed. Among those topics was also the topic of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Agenda item 2, I'll read it for you, is: "Reports on the financing problems in the Army of Republika Srpska." Those are the specifically focusing on the financing problems of the army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were never entirely able to deal with the financing of the army without including everything that I have said previously. Regardless of whether this was discussed at that meeting or not, this is something that I know very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But Mr. Traldi focuses on this meeting and he'll now continue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that completes my questions about this meeting. I believe the previous document, 65 ter 02538, is also an associated exhibit and should get a D number at this time. It's a relatively brief document and I'd suggest that it be admitted in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D631, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D631 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To close this topic, sir, in the Karadzic case when you were shown this document, you testified in the pertinent part --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the reference is 65 ter 31218, page 30, transcript page 38.770 of the Karadzic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- that: "We tried that all the items considered to be war booty be placed at the disposal of the general public good, especially for the defence of the country, the army, et cetera." Do you stand by that testimony today?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct. But it was not just of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I'll turn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, it's good practice in this courtroom that if you quote from a previous testimony that you'd show it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. Can we call up then 65 ter 31218, page 30. And we'll zoom in on lines 18 to 20. And so I'm not sure if Your Honours wish me to repeat the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- but this is the question that I read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but it just allows us, for example, to read the text to the question that the witness at that time responded. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, one more question on the topic of financing of the army. You mentioned that the government sought it from a number of different sources, and you specified Serbia. One of your roles was to meet with representatives of Serbia and of Montenegro to procure assistance for the Republika Srpska including for the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about VRS. You could say the Army of Republika Srpska. Well, no. I discussed many topics with them. Most frequently the topic of refugees and then, of course, certain forms of assistance. Of course they were asking certain materials from us in return and so on and so forth. You probably cannot assume that we in Republika Srpska after the Croats and Muslims left the JNA, we had more pieces of weaponry than the number of the population. We sold part of that weaponry, even to Serbia. Serbia would buy from us semi-manufactures.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I take it your answer to my question, whether you met with representatives of Serbia and Montenegro to procure assistance for the Republika Srpska including for the VRS, is, yes, you did; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, yes. But mostly it was not like that overall because we spoke about wheat, about harvesting, about the exports of our products to Serbia, and, of course, about certain articles that we needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to a different topic. In paragraph 56 of your statement, you say that Muslims in Cerska and Srebrenica in the early part of 1993 presented what you call a false picture, that they had nothing to eat and no water. Now, you didn't go to Srebrenica yourself during your time as prime minister, did you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There seems to be a mix-up here. This was an intercepted conversation in which I discussed Cerska with Dr. Karadzic where they were saying people there were dieing of hunger. Would you please allow me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I only allow you to continue to speak if you seek to answer the question. The simple question was whether you went to Srebrenica yourself during your time as prime minister. All the rest is what you think may be on the mind of Mr. Traldi, and apparently you already anticipate that you need to defend yourself in one way or another. But just listen to the question: Did you go in that period of time to Srebrenica yourself? Would you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No Serb, including myself, could even dare to think about entering Srebrenica. Had we gone in there, we would have never come out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So when you say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you also next time limit your answer to what really is asked. And that is not whether it was dangerous to go there, it was not whether others went there, but just whether you went there. Would you please focus your answer on the question that is put to you. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So when you say --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you. I see that you want to interrupt me. Other than that, you cannot just say whether I was there. The question should be could I have gone there. So I must give an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The question -- first of all, if I think I have to interrupt you, I'm conducting these proceedings. That's one. Second, you interrupted Mr. Traldi, which you are invited not to do. Third, you can answer the question whether you went there irrespective of whether you had an opportunity, because if you have got no opportunity to go there, the simple answer is, no, I didn't go there. If Mr. Traldi would like to know why you did not go there, he'll certainly ask you. Or in re-examination, perhaps Mr. Lukic will ask you. Please focus your answer on the questions and refrain from, as a matter of fact, what is comment rather than an answer to the question. If there is anything urgent at the end of your testimony which you think it was unfair that you could not say in answer to the questions, I will give you an opportunity, within certain limits, to add anything at the end of your testimony. But for now, focus on the questions. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, sir, when you say in paragraph 56 of your statement that Muslims in Cerska and Srebrenica had food and other reserves and presented a false picture that civilians had nothing to eat and no water in the spring of 1993, you have no direct personal knowledge yourself whether what you're saying there is true or not, do you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had the finding of our army regarding Cerska. And as for Srebrenica, the two associates of Alija Izetbegovic from Srebrenica should be consulted as to what they were writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, again, no personal knowledge yourself as to the condition of Muslim civilians in Srebrenica in March 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I somehow -- okay. It is, actually, wrong presentation of the previous answer. This gentleman had personal knowledge about Cerska from the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's keep this -- let's cut this short. Mr. Traldi, if you have, say, personal knowledge, you can understand that in two ways: Knowledge based on your personal observation of the situation. Another way of understanding personal knowledge is whether you obtained any information which made you knowledgeable about the situation even without personal observation. That, apparently, is the issue. And I do understand that it is your question whether this witness made this statement on the base of his personal observation of the situation or whether he had received information which was not based on personal observation. That, apparently, is the issue you want to raise. Now, by answering the previous question, the witness has more or less answered your question. Because I understood your previous question, Mr. Lukic, that you expressed this opinion on the basis of information you had received from the sources you mentioned and not by personally observing the situation at the spot. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd just refer Your Honours to General Tucker's personal observation in this regard in P317.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's argument, Mr. Traldi. That's not a question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to the exchange commissions. In paragraphs 33 and 42 of your statement, you say when the exchange commissions of the Republika Srpska used the term "civilian prisoners," they were referring to those who were reasonably suspected of committing crimes. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have 65 ter 19597.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document coming from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina's commission for the exchange of POWs dated 10 February 1993. Now, the first paragraph you see refers to girls of Muslim ethnicity who are being detained and abused in a brothel in Miljevina. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to page 5 in the English and 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now we see President Izetbegovic is pardoning a convicted person named Nikola Ostojic. Do you see that as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page, page 6 in the English and 5 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, there are two exchanges on this page and I'm interested in the second one. And we see Mr. Ostojic is being exchanged for a number of people, mostly women. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So in this instance, the only one of the people be exchanged who is suspected of a crime is a Serb who was being held in a Bosnian prison; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say anything about this because I don't know anything about it. Many exchanges were not effected through the government and the government did not know about everything. I really did want to understand this particular one, but I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll ask that this be marked for identification. And I'm -- we'll have occasion to see it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI P6730 [Realtime transcript read in error "P6713"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was also on the Defence list?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, it wasn't, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore a P number will have to be assigned to this document, marking it for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I think I might have heard P6730 rather than 6713.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct. I read the transcript. It should be MFI 6730.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore P6730 is marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now can we have P3808. And this is a document coming from the Republika Srpska exchange commission in October 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, this document will come from Captain Bulajic. You'd appointed him president of the exchange commission; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now -- and looking to the first paragraph, he writes -- and just to note, do you see the "Republika Srpska Central Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners and Civilians" identified at the top of the page? I see you've nodded but you have to articulate your answer for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So he writes: "Since the beginning of the combat activities in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, along with its basic purpose, Butmir KP Dom has also been used as a location for the accommodation of Muslim civilians passing through this facility in transit to the Muslim part of the Sarajevo. This facility was used for this purpose because there are no better conditions, in the area, for Muslim civilians who have been in the process of," and he puts these next two terms in quotes, "'family reunification' or 'freedom of movement', been passing through this part of Republika Srpska on the way to their final destinations in the Muslim part of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina or further on." Now, I'd put to you that Mr. Bulajic is clearly referring to civilians not discussing whether they are suspected of crimes, just referring to regular civilians; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speak about exceptions, but as a rule, all those who were placed in prison did have some reason for being put there, some failing, some errors. I do not exclude the possibility, however, that some of them were innocent and who knows why they were put there. But the rule was that civilians were kept separate from the prisoners, and then prisoners, army prisoners, were also kept separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just looking at the next sentence, he writes: "According to rough estimates, about 10.000 Muslim civilians (of all ages) passed through this facility during the war ..." So we're discussing just Butmir KP Dom. It's your evidence that all 10.000 of those would have some failing or some error that led to them being incarcerated?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't speak about 10.000, but I doubt that figure of 10.000. So that's why I'm reluctant to say anything about it. I mean, can you imagine the number of 10.000 passing through a small prison? I happen to know that it's a small building. I'd never been inside, though. But I don't believe that it was actually the figure of 10.000. You need to be aware that during the war many officers, senior figures, wanted to exaggerate a little bit than it actually was talking about the living, the dead, the captured, the wounded, and so probably that would apply also in this case with the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now if we could just have P4008, briefly. As it comes up, this is an order from General Tolimir issued the 3rd of October 1994. And I'll be looking at the end of paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he writes here: "It should be kept in mind that in the exchanges, we receive captured soldiers of the Republika Srpska while we mostly given them civilians." Now, he isn't referring to people suspected of crimes either. He's just referring to civilians; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's at the end of paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise. There is -- yes, you're correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see it, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it now. I do not recall it at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait for the question, please. We are just ensure that you have read the relevant portion where Mr. Traldi referred you to the wrong paragraph. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I apologise again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So he, too, is referring just to civilians, not to people suspected of crimes; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think the whole document should be read because otherwise the gentleman is misled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- if we start from the paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, any problem in allowing the witness - it's time for a break, anyhow - be given a hard copy so that he can read the whole of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objection at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that a hard copy be made of this document. Mr. Lukic, if you would be so kind to read during the break the whole of this document so as to avoid any confusion, and we'd like to see you back after the break. The hard copy will be provided to you after you've left the courtroom. It's even provided while you're still in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we'll resume at 5 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I might use the time briefly, Mr. President. We've received the English translation for P6728 which was MFI'd yesterday. The translation's been uploaded into e-court under doc ID B0159686ET. And if the Defence agrees, we'd request that the court officer be instructed to attach the translation to the original and that the MFI status be removed and the document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think was it with this -- yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Then the Registrar is hereby instructed to attach the English translation to P06728. After this has been done, P6728 is admitted into evidence. And, Mr. Lukic, as always, you have an opportunity if there is any problem with the translation to -- to report this within 48 hours. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P4008 back up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's still on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Oh, there it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, I understand you reviewed this document over the break. Having reviewed the document --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- I'd put to you, again, that General Tolimir is referring when he says in the fourth paragraph: "... in the exchanges, we receive captured soldiers of the Republika Srpska while we mostly give them civilians." I'd put to you again that he is not referring to people suspected of crimes, just to regular civilians. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, tell me what period this refers to? Is the date I find at the bottom the 4th of October, 1994, correct? I see a similar date at the top, but that I'm uncertain. I can't see it all too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't understand that there is any dispute between the parties that this is a document from October 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, yes, early October 1994 is the date.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was no longer prime minister at the time. I do have other objections vis-à-vis this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you are supposed to answer questions, Mr. Lukic. If there is any challenge to the authenticity and lack of signatures, et cetera, that's left in the hands of the parties. Mr. Traldi, could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to put --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- one more time for the clarity of the record, I'd put to you again he is not referring to people suspected of crimes. He is referring to regular civilians. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would object --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- to the questions. What General Talic was thinking is not to ask this gentleman. And from the military perspective, any civilian incarcerated is civilian. So it doesn't mean -- it just means that they are actually suspected of crimes. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you would say --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- there is no dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This calls for speculation of the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there are two elements. First of all, that if the witness with his knowledge gained in his previous position as prime minister would have any further explanation for the language used here that he has been given an opportunity to do so. That's one. Second is I do establish that apparently there is no dispute between the parties that the reference to civilians here means civilians without any reason to believe that they would have -- suspected of having committed any crimes. Is that well understood, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the commission, the name of the commission I will read it in B/C/S so you get proper translation. I don't have English document here. It says, I quote: [Interpretation]: The Central Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners and Civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is how it is translated. Let's -- I think we are now entering the argument. I do establish that the reference to civilians here is not civilians suspected of any criminal the activities or did I misunderstand you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we read the document, we see that those civilians were transferred from prisons to one prison at one place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you can read the last paragraph of this document. I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll read, one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. If you invite us to do so we'll certainly do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page in English. And, Mr. Lukic, you used the name of General Talic but this is signed by General Tolimir, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I might ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- if the witness could be asked to remove his headphones --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- and perhaps I should have done that before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I noticed that the witness understands the English language, Mr. Traldi. You understand English, don't you? You do understand the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I earlier heard you speak to the usher where you used the word "translation." You remember? At the very start this morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you don't -- if you don't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But my knowledge is very modest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you should have told me that you have a modest knowledge of the English language and you should not have said to me that you don't understand the English language. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yet, I do not understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will take its time to read this document now in its entirety and then you can continue after that, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I'll turn to a different topic now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you'd prefer that we read it during our next break, we'll do so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, actually, Your Honours, I -- I'd fulfilled what I considered putting my case to the witness about the exchange commissions and wouldn't have further questions about this document unless --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- Mr. Lukic wants to go back to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then we already read it anyhow but for different purposes. At least, and let's have a look, this is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to ask you now about some negotiations that you took part in early in your time as prime minister. You took part in negotiations with the Republic of Herceg-Bosna; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you mention in paragraph 70 of your statement that a peace agreement with the Croats was signed. When was that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, it was around mid-1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And before that and shortly after you became prime minister, you were part of the Republika Srpska delegation to the talks in Geneva; right? I'm speaking of the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not go to Geneva.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, perhaps then you can help me understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have P357. This will be one of General Mladic's notebooks. Page 53 in English and 55 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So this is 11 January and we see "a meeting of conference presidents and our delegation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is the B/C/S page the right one?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Clearly not. Could we turn back a page, please. And one more. I'm sorry, I'd given page number for the B/C/S original rather than for the transcript and it's led to some confusion, and that's my error. Can we go back one more page. I say this is -- we're seeing the numbers of the speakers of the meeting here. Okay. So now we've reached the right page, "Meeting of Conference Presidents and our delegation." And if we could just turn now to page 55 in the English and the B/C/S. And could we go back to 54 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So we see a Professor Lukic in the middle of the page explaining the reasons for objecting to a number of points. Now, does that refer to you or to a different Professor Lukic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what meeting this refers to. There were two Professor Lukics. The other Professor Lukic was a legal expert. I don't know which one this refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll look into the matter before the next session, and I may have follow-up questions. But I'll turn to another topic, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can 65 ter 1D02453 be brought to the screen. And this will be the programme of Prime Minister Lukic's government as he presented it to the Republika Srpska Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this was an introduction of you and your government programme to the assembly when you were being confirmed as prime minister; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this speech explains to the assembly what you intended to do in your role as prime minister; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any programme is like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You -- it appears that this is a speech. Did you deliver it yourself?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember. Perhaps I may have given it to someone else to read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say that this programme was prepared in advance and that it had Dr. Karadzic's absolute support. Now, did Mr. Karadzic provide his support to your programme in advance of the speech being given?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many people had the programme, including members of the government. Some ministers, some deputies. And, yes, of course I provided it to Mr. Karadzic first before giving it to anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I'd like to look at three particular points in your programme. Now, first here on page 1 in English and B/C/S in the third paragraph, we read: "The most pressing task of the government I am proposing will be to complete the project of statehood for the Serbian people. The time is right for us to be able to protect most successfully and efficiently the vital interests of our people with the internal strength of the state which we are building. This state will be integrated into other Serbian states as much as possible." Now, by "other Serbian states," you meant the Republic of Serbian Krajina and Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Praise God, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning now to page 5 in the English and the top of page 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Below the words "honourable deputies," we see you note: "In the last two years, many Serbian families from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Slovenia and Croatia have been left without their homes and hearths. This government must immediately take care of their accommodation and permanent settlement. We already have the space and preconditions to resolve this urgent problem since we have a number of municipalities with very low population density." Now, permanently resettling displaced Serbs in territory under your government's control was part of your programme as you set it out to the assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now looking to page 8 in the English and page 6, paragraph 1 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We also see --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we're at the top of the page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "The government will give more support and assistance" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should make sure that the right B/C/S page is on the screen. I doubt that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we turn back to the previous page. So my Cyrillic, I'm afraid, is limited. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: My doubt was based on the length of the two paragraphs above the words "honourable deputies."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we turn back to page 6 for a moment in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's the right page. Mr. Lukic agrees. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now and then, my notes are accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Looking at the top of the page, we read: "The government will give more support and assistance than it has done so far to the research, gathering of documentation and presentation to the world of war crimes that are being committed against the Serbian people. At the same time, we will also insist on the request that judicial and law enforcement organs carry out preparations and investigations. Perpetrators of crimes do not deserve to be forgiven." So documenting and investigating crimes against Serbs was also a part of your government's programme; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'd put to you that if we review this speech, we will not see any mention of permanently resettling Muslim and Croat refugees in the territory of Republika Srpska, will we?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we will not see any mention of investigating crimes committed against Muslims or Croats, will we?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Should I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think you've answered my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But if the Chamber wishes a further explanation, I'll leave it in their hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to give a short explanation, you are invited to do so now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was our position on the basis of conclusions of different commissions that all crimes, no matter who perpetrated them, had to be registered and processed. We did not divide crimes into Serbian, Muslim, or Croatian crimes, let alone anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to follow-up on the topic you've just mentioned. Now the prosecution and investigation of crimes was often discussed at government sessions; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, it was sufficient bearing in mind the circumstances and other problems faced by the government. The word "often" was used, but it would be difficult to achieve for a government engaged in a war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to look at a few examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But before I do, this is a relatively brief document. It's one of those that the Defence has tendered as an associated exhibit and I'd ask that it be assigned a D number and admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have -- one second, please. You say it's a relatively -- you are referring to the document we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The one that remains on our screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter number 1D2453 will be Exhibit D632.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D632 is admitted. Now, I didn't know whether you were talking about a new document or whether it was about the document we just looked at. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. Could we have 65 ter 1D02461.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is the 63rd Session of the Republika Srpska government held on the 5th of February 1993, a few weeks after you announced your programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 15 in the B/C/S and 10 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And direct your attention to point 10. And we see that: "It was concluded that the Ministry of the Interior and the republican public prosecutor's office gather information on the criminals and crimes committed against the Serbian people and to publish it in the media." So my question to you is, again, here, we're seeing a reference to crimes committed specifically against Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can 65 ter 07340 [Realtime transcript read in error "3740"] be brought to the screen. This is the 71st Session of the government. And I believe it's early March 1994. Could we have page 8 in the B/C/S and 12 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see at item 20 the government taking notice of a report of the work of the state documentation centre for the investigation of crimes against -- specifically against Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is what is in the document, then, yes, in all likelihood.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in that discussion, it says towards the end of the second item of paragraph 20 that: "It is of special importance to instigate criminal proceedings against individual and group perpetrators of crimes and genocide against the Serbian people. The media should report these proceedings and give them an appropriate level of publicity both at home and abroad." This is consistent with the platform that you sent out to the assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evidently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, both of these are associated exhibits and I'd ask that they be given D numbers. They are minutes and so I wouldn't have an objection to them being marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well -- only I don't know if we have the right document. You called for 3740 and said that it's 71st session, so I think it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It certainly attempted to say 7340.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So that's why I don't know if we have the right document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We do. The transcript simply misrecorded me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I am quite sure that's my fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We have the right document and I've discussed the part that I meant to discuss and it is an associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, 65 ter 1D02461, 63rd session of the Republika Srpska government, receives number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D633 MFI, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D633 is MFI'd. Is there -- is that because we still have to make a selection, Mr. Traldi, that it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's why I was offering. I'm in your hands as to whether to mark it for identification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- or admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And again, how many pages is the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: D2461? I'm afraid it's not in my notes. I can say, Mr. Lukic, referring to General Mladic's counsel, and I had discussed making a selection from that document yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. It's -- in the English it's 23 pages, but we looked only, I think, at two or three pages including the cover page. Therefore, it is MFI'd. The next one is 65 ter 7340 receives number --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be exhibit D634 MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D634 is MFI'd. The number of pages is --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think approximately the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you'll -- you'll sit together and you'll inform the Chamber later whether we need only an excerpt or whether we need the whole of the document. For the time being, it's MFI'd as D634. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 40 of your statement you refer to the Republika Srpska government forming a commission to investigate war and other crimes. I want to look at the genesis of that commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 16760. This is the 67th session of the government held on the 6th of April 1993. And if we could look at page 5 in both languages, item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, it notes that an extensive debate was held regarding the investigation and establishing of crime and genocide against members of the Serb people and refers at the end of that first paragraph to the state documentation centre which has already been set up. And then refers to setting up an authoritative commission which would exclusively deal with the issue. Do you see that text? And again, you have to articulate your answer for the record.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now turning to task 3, we see --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Starting on page 7 in the English and 6 on the B/C/S. I'll wait for it to come up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "It was agreed to set up a Commission which would ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we'll turn to the next page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That this commission would "prepare a suit on the genocide committed over members of the Serb people, ensure that the suit was pled before all relevant factors. The commission would likewise work on preparing a response to the suit for an alleged genocide committed by the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia." Now, that latter suit was the lawsuit which was brought by the Bosnia and Herzegovina against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at the International Court of Justice; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is our commission that had the task that you referred to earlier. I don't know why now you are also bringing in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, we see it mentioned here at this meeting. So one of the purposes of investigations into war crimes by your government was to prepare to respond to the genocide suit brought against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just information, but we did not take any measures to investigate anything that had to do with that. I don't, at least, remember that being one of our tasks. We were speaking only about our victims. We formed our own commission and that was its task. Everything else was incidental and not important as far as we were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is another associated exhibit. I'd ask that it be -- again, I'm in your hands and Mr. Lukic's as to whether to mark it or admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the document would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D635 MFI'd, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D635 is MFI'd. If a selection is further made, it should include not only the portion you read but the whole of that item in the, I think it was on page 2 and 3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We would have intended to include at the minimum the whole of items 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That should be done at least --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Along with what he referred to in his statement, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we wait for the further information to be provided by the parties. Please proceed, meanwhile, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, could the Prosecution have 65 ter 1D02470. And this is an excerpt from the Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this is the publication of the commission establishing that commission; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask that it be assigned a D number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D636, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D636 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then I want to look at a document, 65 ter 1D02488.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this is a report from your commission from March 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, here on the first page in the B/C/S but the second page on the English ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read: "On 2 March 1994, the Commission sent its first Work Report to the Government which said that the Commission had processed the submitted documents and identified 528 Muslims and Croats who had committed war crimes." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The document then notes reports just below that from various judicial organs, public prosecutors offices and lower courts. And then it analyses those documents, which I would like to go through quickly. At point A --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- it notes that the Brcko documents identified 759 Muslims and Croats who had allegedly committed crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning to page 5 in the English and 4 in the B/C/S. Point B.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It notes that from Zvornik there were reports that allegedly 215 Muslims had committed crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 9 in the English, 7 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Point C -- refers to an investigation in Bijeljina into two Muslims. And just below that, point D, Vlasenica, investigations into 26 Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 10 in the English, 8 in the B/C/S. And there is no point E recorded in the document. But you can see in the English in the middle of the page, and in the B/C/S I believe it's also at the beginning of the long paragraph, a discussion of Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it refers to a report about 53 Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then turning to page 11 in the English and the bottom of page 8 in B/C/S, point F.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Five Muslim suspects in Sarajevo. Now, I'd put to you that that adds up to reports against more than a thousand Muslim suspects; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I know how many of which persons in the entire report, the report cited by locations, towns, places, how many people were killed in each of those locations? And it referred to the numbers of Serbs, Muslims, and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Referred to the number of suspects, didn't it? Muslims and Croats. Let's go back and we can look at the examples more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So let's start on point 2 in both languages. Sorry, page 2 in both languages, point A. And let's just zoom in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So here, the Brcko public prosecutor's office has sent documents identifying Muslims and Croats who allegedly committed war crimes; right? They are identified specifically as Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It would be ridiculous for me to take a report such as it is. I can take it as correct or not, but I cannot alter it or speak about it in terms of it being positive or negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to do that at the moment. What I'm asking you to do is confirm that here in the text it refers to the reports as being specifically against Muslims and Croats. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand it as if you were defending the crimes from the Muslim and Croat people --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and I'm simply in way taking Serbs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] You are not invited to enter into a debate with Mr. Traldi. Mr. Traldi puts it to you that at least in this report where a large number of crimes are described, that it is exclusively crimes committed by Croats and Muslims or -- Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just, just -- Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting. I was putting the sections I had referred to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- were exclusively Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it would have been fair to the witness that you would have mentioned them all, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was getting to the next one on the list, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So Mr. Traldi puts it to you that a large number, and I think you talked about a thousand approximately --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My mental math says between a thousands and 1100, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That over a thousand of the cases mentioned in this report are cases of crimes comitted by Muslims and Croats, whether you would agree with that or not. And then he'll follow-up on other matters in the same report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's difficult to be in my place. I know villages where people were killed. I know. I was working there. So I really know what it's all about. So I cannot stand behind one or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if anybody is having any doubts, only I would say that this needs to be checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the simple question was that the cases referred to by Mr. Traldi amount to over a thousand, and that those exclusively deal with crimes committed by Muslims and Croats. Whether you have any comment on that -- whether other crimes were committed is perhaps a matter we may look at later or in further -- in re-examination, but we are just at this moment talking about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, sir, speaking only of the numbers as they are reflected in the report, I'm not asking you about the truth or falsity of any allegations. I'd put to you again we've seen reports against more than a thousand suspected Muslim or Croat perpetrators in this report; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that as being excessive in view of the fact that I know of crimes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi. Next question. The Chamber is in a position to verify whether the number you refer to is accurate, yes or no, and whether it amounts to a thousand or more. And it's clear that the witness says that he cannot confirm whether this is truthful reporting yes or no. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could go back to page 11 in the English. And turning to page 9 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And here we're going to see a reference to two files regarding crimes committed by Serbs. And if we look at point A in this section, there's two suspects, Nebojsa Lazic and Boro Radic. And it says here that Mr. Radic is dead, and at the end of the paragraph that Mr. Lazic is at large. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I believe that it must be so since somebody has written that that was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so point B below that, Stanko Knezevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 12 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it says also at large; right? Asking only that's what it says in the document. Right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since it is written, I assume that it stands. But I really think that it's impossible, and please believe me, for a president or prime minister to know who was where.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the reason I've been asking you about this document is that in your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have paragraph 85 of the witness's statement on the screen. That's D626, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In your statement you discuss this document, and you discuss it under a different number because your statement was taken for the Karadzic case, and so the Karadzic case number was used. So it's paragraph 85 and it refers to it by the Karadzic number 1D7886. And you say that this commission that was -- that we just saw a report from, its task was to gather documentation on events that could be seen as war crimes, and you say at the end of the paragraph: "The commission processed reports of crimes committed by Serbs as well."
