And so my question is: When you said that, you meant to refer to two reports of crimes by Serbs of which none of the alleged perpetrators had been arrested; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in a position to know whether somebody was arrested or not. All I was able to do was to use the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I think that what Mr. Traldi puts to you is that the document says that they are not arrested, at least they are not reported as being arrested. And one of the suspects having been killed. And you're commenting on a document. So that's what Mr. Traldi puts to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only believe it. I don't have any other information. I didn't gather any other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have the document back. And it's 1D2488. I'll be asking again for page 11 and -- sorry, page 12 in the English and 9 in the B/C/S. And just below the portions we've reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we read: "On 18 March 1994, members of the War Crimes Committee of the Federal Government of Yugoslavia visited the Republika Srpska Commission for Gathering Information on Crimes Committed against Humanity and International Law. On that occasion it was agreed to make the documentation gathered by our Commission available to this Committee, because 'Yugoslavia' (Serbia and Montenegro) was to draft a response to the application filed with the International Court of Justice on 20 March 1993 by the so-called Republic of BH." That's the genocide suit that we discussed earlier; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for genocide but for the participation in the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll seek agreement with the Defence on the legal characterisation of the suit rather than pursuing it further. But if we could turn now to the next page in both languages. And -- sorry, one more I'm afraid. And I'm looking for the struck-through text after the numeral 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this struck-through text refers to an Annex 2, a document on the "Extent of the violations of the human rights of women as a new form of war crime in Croatia and BiH," by Mario Nobilo. And it refers a few lines below that to a report by Tadeusz Mazowiecki.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I apologise for my pronunciation of that name to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Special Rapporteur of the commission of human rights. Do you see that text?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now it appears that the commission, at least, was aware of and had reviewed the reports. Do you know whether that's true?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably is. I can't say it is not. But I can't say it is, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your government was aware of those reports as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part I think they were informed, but I doubt they studied the texts in depth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For the moment without looking in too much depth, you were aware that Mr. Nobilo and Mr. Mazowiecki alleged that large scale crimes had been committed by Serb forces in Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was standard practice coming from Croatia and the rest of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Claims were always that no matter what crime was committed, it was committed by Serbs. However, Nobilo did not mention how many crimes were perpetrated by Croats, and I won't he was touch upon the topic of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd request that this document receive a D number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, before we further deal with it, that the red markings and the striking through originate from where? And perhaps looking at you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I'm addressing Counsel Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I only can guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it was on your list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] it has our ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it was included in the statement. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not our marking for sure. I can assure that it's not our marking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but if you -- if you intend to have a document admitted as an associated exhibit, if that's how I have to understand it, then at least you should be aware of a document where others have made markings, et cetera, who made them, and for what purpose, and why the striking through is there. Who made the emphasis by the red squares? I've seen them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Karadzic Defence would usually make those red --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- squares.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand that that is a way of a type -- a way of drawing the attention to a specific portion. The striking through, however, is of a different --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to supplement that information, I think I can probably confirm what Mr. Lukic is suggesting the original version of the document in our system has the strike-through but does not have the red marking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is useful additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D637, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D637 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed -- no, please do not proceed. That's -- Witness, we'll take a break and we'll resume at 20 minutes past 12.00. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I could make use of this time. We do now tender 65 ter 08282c with respect to the map that was used during Mr. Bukva's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which was marked -- no, let me see. Yes, it needs a new number because it's a special portion of P2952. Mr. Registrar, the number for 65 ter 08282c would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6731, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution have 65 ter 31239. Now, we have not received the translation for this yet, but this is a letter dated the 7th of January 1993 from the permanent representative of Croatia to the United Nations, addressed to the Secretary General.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mario Nobilo's name appears. And it refers to the extent of violation of women's human rights and raping as a new type of war crime in Bosnia-Herzegovina as an attachment. Now, that's the report that before the break you confirmed that the commission and your government were aware of it but might not have studied the text in detail; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm certain they did not go into the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I'm just going to ask if some of the allegations in the report were known to you. And I'm asking -- I'm going to ask specifically whether you knew those things were alleged to have happened. Can we agree to proceed in that fashion?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know quite a lot about it. The first thing I know is that the Croats were the ones who committed the first crimes in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the first women to be raped were the women of Posavina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you again. What I asked was if you would agree, as we go through the report, that we would simply discuss whether you were aware of the allegations that were being made there. Not whether they were true or false and not about crimes by another side. So can we proceed simply by discussing whether you were aware that particular things had allegedly happened?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last war all such things happened on all sides. However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it was particularly often done by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I stop you again. You are giving sweeping statements about crimes committed by others, whereas you are asked a question: Whether you were aware of these allegations. True or not, whether others did even more horrible things, and this Chamber has heard evidence about quite a number of incidents, many sides. But the question now is whether you were aware of these allegations. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I'm going to look at a couple of specific allegations in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's just a one-page document, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We appear not to have the attachment uploaded, so I'll come back to this document. And I'm going to ask that we have 65 ter 1D02467 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this will be a letter from you to the VRS Main Staff and the command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. Now, looking at the beginning of this letter, you write: "The Government of Republika Srpska has been informed that there are cases of looting, killing, setting fire to buildings and rape in the municipality of Novo Sarajevo (Grbavica), committed mostly by members of the Army of Republika Srpska. "We have reliable information that the looted equipment and goods are transported mostly by military trucks." And then you demand that measures be taken. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And below that you write: "The above measures also need to be taken in other areas in similar cases." So you were aware that similar types of crime were happening elsewhere; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't aware of that. When certain reports were made whenever there was any doubt, we reacted in this or similar fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, these reports were reports that the crimes were being committed by soldiers of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. In that Army of Republika Srpska, there were many who simply used the military uniform to do what they liked, whereas at the same time, they were basically not members of the armed forces. We asked the armed forces to deal with all such people who wore military uniforms doing the things we cite here. I knew some of such things but not all. It was under that presumption that we drafted this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. What you characterise the perpetrators as in this document is members of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we always did that whenever they were in military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, your government had discussed around this time these crimes, these types of crimes, being committed by soldiers; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And for reference, that's in 65 ter 16760, which may have a D number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This wasn't the first time that you'd informed General Mladic or General Galic of soldiers committing crimes in Novo Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. If there are such documents in existence, it is true. In any case, we never thought that the entire armed forces in general were involved. We could not cherry-pick such individuals. We just wanted the army to find the soldiers involved in such matters. That was our goal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now if we could have Exhibit P346, and I'll be asking for page 157 in the English and 159 in the B/C/S. And this is one of General Mladic's notebooks. And this previous document I'd ask be given a D number that's an associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 1D2467 will be D638.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D638 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So here we see what's identified as meeting with Prime Minister Lukic on the 25th of March 1993, and you identify some problems; theft, profiteering, looting, desire to acquire wealth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 158 in the English. And I believe we need the next page in the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Greed, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you inform him: "Some soldiers rape even Serbian women (in Grbavica) ..." And that you yourself had taken someone who'd done this out of Sarajevo. So you had reached out to General Mladic and General Galic after these crimes had begun to be directed as Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid you're asking too much. What General Mladic noted down -- well, I have no reason to doubt its accuracy. But what bothers me is the word "even." I don't think I would have used it. But even if I had, those who raped did not care who was who. It is true that there was a soldier who is no longer among the living, and I did not want to mention his name, who raped each and every woman he came across. He was transferred to our territory in Romanija and he was killed. His colleagues at a check-point placed close to my apartment told me that it should have been done a long time ago. So they, too, condemned his behavior. If that had not been a problem, it would not have been tackled. There was also corruption, profiteering, and so on and so forth. It is true that it accompanies every war. In any case, I believe our positions were such that we had to make sure we were aware of those things happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution have 65 ter 31222.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And here we see a report from you as prime minister to the Sarajevo CSB and the Sarajevo Romanija Corps security service. And you're again referring to reports of crime in Novo Sarajevo including robbery, rape, and other violent activities from which even citizens of Serbian ethnicity are not spared. So you're again expressing concern that crime has started to be directed against Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe your understanding is too narrow-minded and drastic. Those who did such things did not care if the woman in question was a Serb, Croat, or Muslim. They did it dishonourably, and it wouldn't even occur to any of us that women should be raped no matter whether they were Serb or Muslim. This just means taking things out of context and to rely on simple words or to provide opinions does not meet the threshold in terms of why we are here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're saying that Mr. Traldi is misinterpreting it, but could you then explain why you did not write that robbery, rape, and other violent activities took place? It's in this letter that specifically reference is made to citizens of Serbian ethnicity as being victims, not exclusively, but it's the letter who draws the attention to the ethnicity of victims. Any comment on why you did not write in neutral terms that these crimes are committed without any reference to ethnicity of the victims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps what we wanted to stress was that these people were indeed greedy -- well, Serb women enjoyed a certain level of protection. And when such people raped them, or even them, it means that they really didn't care about a thing in the world. Such things are not necessarily best discussed in forums such as this one, but I can tell you that many people, first and foremost Serbs, reacted fiercely to it. They were in constant communication with the MUP, with the army, with the head of municipality, and so on, and they insisted on doing so until the problem was dealt with. Fortunately, and I don't know whether it was by sheer circumstance, was that the few who were involved in such activities were shortly afterwards killed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- on front lines. So I tend to believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not, was not part of my question, whether those suspected were killed or not. Could you explain to us, please. You said Serb women enjoyed a certain level of protection. What was the level of protection which Serb women enjoyed which other women did not enjoy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First and foremost, their husbands were there in our armed forces, in our police, or worked for the municipality, et cetera. That was the fact. And that kind of protection came from that source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would Serb police officers in any way less protect other women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a rule, I don't think they would protect them any less. Especially if I am reminded of the people I know. They would protect all women equally and they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P6732, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6732 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I understand that we now have the full version of the document I tried to use a moment ago. If we could have 65 ter 31239a. We've gone through the cover page, so if we could have page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And looking at the lower section, under the word "Timing," about halfway down in the paragraph, Mr. Nobilo is writing: "After 2 April 1992 (i.e. after the outbreak of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina) mass rapings of predominantly Muslim women became a widespread phenomenon in Bosnia and Herzegovina." My question is simply: Were you aware during your time as prime minister that there were allegations and reports of mass rapings of Muslim women in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And actually, Mr. President, I wonder if it might be an appropriate time for a 90(E) caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may, this is not the right time to warn our witness. You can ask him, I'm sure, anything on this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I consulted with my colleague, Mr. Traldi. From what we see now, that's not, as far as we can see, whatever we have seen before. For that reason -- but of course we are not familiar with the entire document, but it's about knowledge of the witness of reports. That's what it's about which at this moment seems not to justify a 90(E) warning. Unless there is any -- we'll carefully listen to your next questions and we'll also carefully look at the documents you are referring to during your questions to see whether that triggers any further need for Rule 90(E).

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was because I'd been moving from general to somewhat more concrete allegations. I'd --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- requested it, but I'm in the Chamber's hands, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment, the Chamber finds no reason to give a Rule 90(E) warning. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, it's not a 90(E) warning but it's a 90(E) information. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just to briefly restate my question for clarity: Were you aware that it was alleged and reported that mass rapes of Muslim women had occurred in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened in all of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but I'm pretty familiar with the situation in Sarajevo. I can tell you that very few people know Sarajevo as well as I do. This statement is inaccurate. Totally inaccurate. I guarantee you --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that in Sarajevo Serb, Muslim, and Jewish women were being raped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, if one group is mass raped, that does not mean that other groups were not mass raped. That's one. Second, you were not asked about whether allegations were true. You were asked about whether you were aware of these allegations and reports having been made. Were you aware or were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of our opponents kept saying that it was only the Serbs who raped. I know Sarajevo and I know that more Serb women were raped there than Muslim women.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please. I spoke to dozens of women.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to interrupt you. If you continue to refuse to limit your answers to what is asked, this might at a certain point invalidate your testimony. Again, whether true or not, whether expressed by opponents or not, the question was whether you were aware of allegations and reports about the rapes as described here. Were you or were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did hear of them just as many Serbs from the area heard of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to the top of page 3, starting at the end of the second line, we read: "... mass rapings occurred in the initial phase of ethnic cleansing in those areas from which Muslims and Croats were later completely expelled (Bijeljina, Zvornik, Foca, Visegrad, Prijedor, Kozarac, Doboj, Modrica)." Are those allegations you were also aware of, sir? And by that, I mean specifically that rapes had occurred in those areas and that Muslims and Croats had been expelled from those areas.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there and I really didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm asking you if you were aware that it was alleged that this had happened.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's another matter. Wherever the Serbs were at war with Muslims, they asserted that we raped Muslim women, killed them, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And were you also aware of allegations that Muslims and Croats had been expelled from areas including the ones I just identified?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I was aware. I had heard it. I had worked at UNPROFOR. I heard it there. I heard it afterwards. It was not just them who were expelled but all three ethnic groups would be expelling each other, or to put it more clearly, people also were escaping because they were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask that this document be marked for identification pending the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P6733 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the status the document now has. It's marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, we looked at your programme as prime minister earlier, and we saw that one of the components of it was the permanent resettlement of Serb refugees in areas of the Republika Srpska. Two ministers, Velibor Ostojic and Radislav Brdjanin, were tasked to prepare a programme for the accommodation of refugees; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, again, I'm just going to look at a couple of the minutes of government discussions about that programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could is start with 65 ter 07341.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This will be the 68th session of your government in April of 1993. Sorry, I should say the 68th session of the RS government.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask for page 4 in the English and 12 in the B/C/S. Item 35. And for the record this has been given D630, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, item 35 refers to an extensive discussion regarding the materials which were prepared by the minister without a portfolio and which were regarding the organisation and activities and measures to be taken for the return of Serb refugees to the territory of the Republika Srpska. That was the purpose of the programme that Ministers Ostojic and Brdjanin were working on; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 31243. This will be the 69th session of the government. And I'll ask for page 4 in English, 5 in the B/C/S, item 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So we read here that the government reviewed the issue of the accommodations of refugees comprehensively, and starting on the fourth line in the English, the minutes reflect: "The issue of the accommodation of refugees should be resolved primarily and, as a matter of special importance, the factual situation should be created in the population levels in towns and settlements" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're reading, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'll try to do so a little bit slower, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "... towns and settlements which are planned to remain in our Republic. This refers to the towns and settlements on the rim of our Republic, particularly in the territories which are the main directions of linking some regions of the Republic with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia." Then in paragraph 4, it notes: "It was agreed that a separate plan for the accommodation of refugees will be made. It will contain the measures that need to be taken immediately, as well as those of long-term character, designed to resolve the status of refugees, enable their protection by the state, and stimulate their permanent settlement in the places where they arrive." So what we're seeing here, again, is a discussion of the permanent settlement of Serb refugees in these territories; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could not take everybody on a permanent basis. A number of refugees stayed with us, and that is the number that we were thinking of. Some moved to Serbia, and then also another part of the refugees were moving abroad. So it wasn't as simple as it was presented on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So not all of the refugees could be accommodated permanently. The effort was to accommodate some Serb refugees on a permanent basis; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, here again in the documents we've looked at, we don't see any mention of resettling Muslim or Croat refugees; do we?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have Muslim refugees for the most part in our area. They went to the other side. Those that did stay behind or that we had, they were in their houses and their apartments.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P6734 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And keep this status up until then. For the time being, it is about -- why is it marked for identification, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To make a selection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To make a selection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. The Chamber will further hear from the parties. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, could we have 65 ter 02391. This will be the transcript of the 39th Assembly of the Republika Srpska. If we could have page 168 in the English and 135 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Minister Ostojic is speaking. And he starts by saying: "Mr. Chairman, gentlemen members, although the issue of the refugees has been raised many times here, I want to point out the complexity of this problem that has to be prioritised." Now, I don't have any questions for you about that sentence, I'm simply reading it so that it's clear what he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now turning to the end of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He notes: "We have to deal with this problem first in order to establish the geographic continuity of the Serbian population in RS area."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then turning to the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He says: "There are four areas that are extremely sensitive and which should be worked on." And he mentions five, actually. Old Herzegovina, Birac, Posavina, Sana Una area, and Vrbas. And he explains where those areas fall and then says: "We lack the population." So first, these were areas where efforts were being made to permanently resettle those Serbs refugees; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Ostojic's opinion because there was no real possibility for this, and later I will say why. So what Ostojic was saying you would need to take with a large degree of reserve because I guarantee that none of his proposals was ever implemented, neither at the assembly nor the government or any other organs, and you would hear all sorts of things from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's Minister Ostojic who you appointed, along with Minister Brdjanin, to be in charge of the refugee programme; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So he's speaking of an area of his authority; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could not implement anything because people did not trust him very much. He didn't have the -- well, it's not all right even to talk about it much. He's dead now. But I can tell you how he and two other people came to see me, asking for solutions, and I can explain what sort of misconception he was living in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Were they asking for solutions specifically related to the resettlement of Serb refugees? And I'd ask that you just answer yes or no for the moment.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes. There were no other refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So what sort of solutions did your -- the minister in charge of this programme, ask you for?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came with one or two other men, he asked me that settlements be made. I said, "The land is not a problem. We do have state-owned land. That is something that can be done. But do you know how much it would cost to build a neighbourhood for 1.000, 2- or 10.000 people?" He said, "No, well, not that much." And then I took out from my pocket a calculation and showed him how much it would cost. And then when I multiplied that by the number of refugees, I said, "Ostojic, we are talking about billions. Republika Srpska will not have such billions in peacetime, never mind in the middle of the war." And then we discussed things about refugees, about accommodation. We finished that discussion. A solution for the refugees, if you wish to know, was sought with different municipalities that had a number of reserve apartments or were building a number of residential buildings. So that's how we would resolve that, for the municipality to buy or to buy out a certain number of apartments and that would be just one way of dealing with the numerous problems that we had to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, some of the municipalities that you tried to resolve it with that way were in the areas that Mr. Ostojic mentioned here; right? Those areas again are old Herzegovina, Birac, Posavina, Sana Una area?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are weak municipalities. We would mostly find a base or support in Banja Luka or in Bijeljina, a little bit in Trebinje, and so on and so forth. I don't have to number them all. The municipalities that were, as we say, broke, they were not really able to help anybody much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, by this point, early 1994 is when this assembly session was held, you were aware of the strategic objectives of the Bosnian Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a lot of talk about that but not much came out of it. I was not present at the meeting. I was not in the government at the time. So I heard from others about the strategic goals. I did have a number of conversations, but mostly I heard that from Mr. Karadzic when he once was talking about some of the goals at a government meeting, and then a little bit in more detail at an assembly session. However, I must say that I did not read the original text in the official bulletin until 2006 when I went to testify in the trial against -- relating to the Bosnia-Herzegovina indictment. So I did hear about it before but I read about it in detail when I went, as I said, to testify. And let me add something. Many municipalities also had their own additional objectives, and if one calmly sat and collated them all, you would not just have that number that was cited at the meeting but the number of those objectives would be larger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you've provided a lot of information. What I'd like to do is go back to my original question. By this point in early 1994, you were aware of the six strategic objectives set out by President Karadzic, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that before that I did hear him. So I cannot say that I didn't hear of them. But I can say that I did not read about that in detail. And I said earlier when was the first time that I read them in detail in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, what I was interested in wasn't when you first read them in the Official Gazette but when you first became aware of them, and I understand you have to confirmed that that was before this point in early 1994. That's correct, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in late 1993 or also in 1994. I did hear that both in the government and the assembly sessions. I'm not quite sure about the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the areas that Minister Ostojic has identified you knew to be consistent with the strategic objectives of the Serbian people as set out by President Karadzic; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't quite sure. And they were not quite -- they didn't -- they were not quite the same. They didn't overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, it's very different to say they're not quite the same and that they didn't overlap at all, so I'm just going to look at them very quickly with you. Srbinje, that's what was called Foca before that, right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Srbinje, Visegrad, Rogatica, and then also Vlasenica, Bratunac, and Zvornik. Those are in the area of the Drina River; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Rogatica is not quite along the river Drina. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it in the area --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it in the area, sir, identified as Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's more in the Romanija area. Podrinje, Foca, Gorazde, Visegrad, Bratunac, Zvornik and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Posavina that's in the area of the corridor, right, identified by the second strategic objective?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was -- that's in the direction of Banja Luka, let's say. Let's say that. Posavina lies along the Sava River. It's on the right bank of the Sava.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Una area includes the Una River and the border on the Una was also one of the strategic objectives; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, yes. That could have been Novi Grad or Bosanski Novi as it was called before. Only a part of the Una practically belonged to Republika Srpska and that is this part above Novi all the way down to the confluence and on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask that this document be marked for identification so that we can make a selection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It should get a D number. It's an associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D639 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D639 is MFI'd. I'm looking at the clock, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm in your hands, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I would like to take a break now, but could you tell us on how much more time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I will be most of today but should finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Witness, will you please follow the usher. We'll take a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to conclude, sir, the area that we were discussing before the break. I'd put to you that the refugees that were being permanently resettled and the ones that were being assisted in returning to the Republika Srpska's territory were Serbs. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The greatest percentage of them were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to turn now to discussing the Republika Srpska's objectives for what that territory would include. Bosnian Serb objectives entailed claims to more than 60 per cent of Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speak on the basis of my calculations. The Serbs possessed 63 per cent of BiH territory. If we exclude state-owned property, the percentage was 52 per cent. No matter what calculation was used, they were needed to be accorded at least 11 or 12 per cent of all forested areas. So all in all, they had more than 60 per cent of all property in Bosnia and Herzegovina in their position. There were percentages mentioned during the war about 66 or 67. I discussed the percentage with some people and the highest figure that circulated at the time was at around 67 per cent of the territory which we de facto had in our possession. After NATO bombardment, things developed differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... somewhat more detail about the rational for your calculations than I've asked for, but I think that you've explained your position. Now, the claims to more than 60 per cent of the territory, in your official capacity, you relayed those claims to Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, among other leaders; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only myself but others as well. But I stood by that argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I just want to look at one example quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can 65 ter 31225 be brought to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a letter you sent to the Secretary-General and other leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have page 2 in both languages. And I'm looking at the middle of the page in the English and the third sentence in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You write: "We emphasize that the territory of the Bosnia and Herzegovina have been, during the middle ages, populated only by the Serb people and it has belonged to the Serb middle-aged country ..." Now, you're emphasizing here that you consider Bosnia to historically be Serb territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And below that you write: "The structure of the population have changed by the intensive Islamisation and conversion to Catholicism of the Serb people during the rule of Turkey, Venice, and Austria-Hungary. In spite of that, before the Second World War, the Serbs owned 67 per cent of the territory and today they own 64 per cent of the territory of the former socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." So you're saying here, as you've said a moment ago in testimony, that you believe the Serbs to be entitled to 64 per cent or more of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although I was aware of this, I never believed it should be implemented because I always believed other ethnicities had to live there as well and that no one should be driven away or destroyed. Here, as well as in Dayton, we did present maximalist requests but the result is well known to everyone. The other side -- the other sides had similar requests as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we see the end of this document in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document, 65 ter 31225.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P6735, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now turning to some specific territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd like to look at 65 ter 31215.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This will be an interview with you in the VRS magazine "Srpska Vojska."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm looking at the middle column of page 1 towards the bottom in the B/C/S. And page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you're in the course of explaining why you oppose the Vance-Owen Plan, and you say: "At least 40 per cent of the Serbs would be under alien rule. For example, the surrounds of Sarajevo, Birac, Posavina, the municipalities of Krupa na Uni, Novi Grad, Prijedor, and Sanski Most, where the Serbs are in the majority and where they have more than 50 per cent of the territory, would be under Muslim rule." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that. I don't need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your position at the time was that those territories needed to be under Serb rule; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, neither Prijedor nor Sanski Most were Serb majority municipalities before the war, were they?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. The Serbs were in the majority before the slaughtering which took place in both Sanski Most and Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say "before the slaughtering," which war are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Second World War, when I observed the slaughtering involving five-and-a-half-thousand Serbs and 50 Jews. I was only eight years old at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was your position that in part because of what had happened during the Second World War these area had to be under Serb control; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of that and because the Serbs were in the majority. The elections in 1990 showed that the Serbs were in the majority in both Sanski Most and Prijedor. I won't even go into any details about the slaughter in Prijedor which took place in World War II.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender 65 ter 31215.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P6736, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just as to who was the majority in those municipalities, could Prosecution have P3853. And this is a report from CSB Banja Luka in 1995. And it's from the Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior office in Banja Luka. If we could have page 6 at the bottom in English and the top in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, sir, this document's going to include both 1991 and 1995 figures. What I'm interested in at the moment are the 1991 figures before the war. So the RS MUP is reporting that 1991 Prijedor, 42.45 per cent Serbs, 43.97 per cent Muslims, 5.6 per cent Croats. So that's not a Serb majority municipality, is it, according to the RS MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please look at the statute when the assembly was being established in Prijedor. You will see in the statute that the Serbs were in the majority; hence, they assumed power. They could not have without being in the majority. The same is the case with Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's look at Sanski Most too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Page 8 at the top in English and page 7 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the RS is MUP is saying that as of 1991, Sanski Most Serbs 42.2 per cent, Muslims 47 per cent, Croats 7 per cent. So again, the RS MUP is saying that as of 1991, Sanski Most was not a Serb majority municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not right. They would not have been able to come to power. All those who were put in power had to have been in the majority. The situation was the same in Sanski Most and Prijedor. Check it yourself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You make a clear distinction between any outcome of any voting and the ethnic composition as declared by those being asked. Now, I do not know exactly this report, whether it's how people declared themselves or not. I also do not know what you are referring to, that you say you can't be in power. I mean, if all the others are voting in favour of Serb parties --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, for Sanski Most that would not have helped out sufficiently because it was 1.65 per cent. If you add that to 42.20 per cent, you're still not yet at the level of the Muslim percentage. So there, at least, from mathematically, it doesn't explain it. But if you say they could not have been anything else than the majority because they had the power, that certainly needs more explanation. And perhaps Mr. Lukic will assist you in bringing that evidence. Or do you say these numbers are inaccurate? That's another possible explanation. That you say, well, whatever they say here, it's the -- Banja Luka SJB, I think it was, is just wrong in -- with their numbers, which is, of course, another possible explanation. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sanski Most is no longer of relevance nowadays because the Muslims are in power there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serbs, for the most part, left Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we are talking about the 1991 situation and what is relevant or not relevant is at this moment defined by the questions that are put to you. Therefore, if you want to explain Sanski Most any further, please focus on the 1991 figure and don't tell us that it's not relevant because I'd like to know. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1990, the Serbs assumed power in Sanski Most and in Prijedor. Mr. Karadzic has the statute of the municipality of Prijedor from 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Separate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is unaware of the Statute, what exactly it is the witness refers to. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but if we look to the document there is no any kind of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second please. One second please. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no -- not any kind of authorisation of this document. It's some kind of copy with no stamp, with no signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's a -- you say we are contesting the authenticity of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do. There is no number, either. So this is not a document that would be usually produced with -- inside any organ, especially not police with no number, no authorisation, no signature, nothing whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't have the provenance information at my finger tips but I'll provide it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- as soon as it's available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait for that. When I addressed Mr. Lukic, I addressed Counsel Lukic, Mr. Lukic, and I am aware that it may create confusion now and then. Again, the statute the witness was talking about is, as far as I am aware, unknown to the Chamber or at least it is -- or doesn't ring a bell immediately as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know this -- I know it. I saw it some time in the Stakic case but I don't have it on me now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then if that sheds any further light on the testimony of the witness, then, of course, the Chamber would like to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And thanks to people a little bit more skillful than I am, we can already provide provenance about this document that is currently on the screen which was recovered from the Banja Luka CSB in February 1998. The Banja Luka CSB being who the cover page purports to have authored the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, whether it's a final document or not, what we now know is that it apparently was located in the CSB offices in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm happy to review the relevant portions of the census with Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we are --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- by that I mean the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if we are talking about 1991, of course, then the census as a source of information may be available as well. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were talking about how the Serbs came to power in both those areas. In fact in Prijedor, Serbs took over power in late April 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am unaware of that. All I know is how they came to power after the voting process.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31220. This is a document signed for Mr. Lukic and sent to the Prijedor assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you see the date 30th of April, 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this text says: "Please accept my heartiest congratulations on the anniversary of the take-over of power and defence of the Serbian people of the Municipality of Prijedor." Does this refresh your recollection as to whether you were aware that power was taken over by the Serbs in Prijedor on the 30th of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was assumed --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- assumed one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. One second. I was addressing counsel. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can call me Branko today. It is assumed that Mr. Lukic, Professor Lukic, is author of this document, but I think that he already answered before my objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Actually, it wasn't assumed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I said it was signed for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Signed for him. That's the literal text Mr. Traldi used. So perhaps if that is in issue -- well, there was a letter apparently signed for you, Professor Lukic. Does that refresh your recollection in any way about --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the take-over of power in Prijedor in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, I don't remember this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that you were unaware during your time as prime minister of what is termed here the take-over of power and defence of the Serbian people of the municipality of Prijedor as it occurred in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that I don't know, but I don't know in which form, how, when, and where. But I did hear --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- you were aware when you gave the interview we just looked at, so I'm speaking of 1993 now, May 1993, that large numbers of non-Serbs had left Prijedor, Sanski Most, and some of the other areas you described since the beginning of the war; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that. Others knew it. And was it wasn't just in these places. Serbs were leaving in many other places as well. So this was a well known thing throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to stop you at this moment and I'll explain to you what your role is as a witness here. You've given a statement. In that statement, many things are described, including misbehaviour, crimes committed by Muslims, by Croats. There is a strong emphasis on those horrible events. Now, if Mr. Traldi asks you questions which he intends sheds some light on another part of the history, then there is no need to again and again refer to what is already in evidence; that is, that others may have misbehaved as well in evidence through your statement. Therefore, if you emphasize again and again that it's unbalanced what others say, please be aware that what Mr. Traldi is doing is first of all to test the probative value of the evidence you gave in your statement; and second, perhaps shed a different light on some of the events you describe as well. Now, leave that to the parties, leave it to Branko Lukic to specifically address matters which you find very important apparently to address, and leave it to Mr. Traldi to test that evidence, to challenge it to the extent he considers that's necessary, and to give, according to the Prosecution's view, another balance than the one apparently you consider to be the right one. Leave that to the parties and refrain from further again and again imposing what, in your view, the balance is rather than to answer the questions that are put to you. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P6737, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, your government conducted a census in 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the Chamber has received evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- showing that "Kozarski Vjesnik" in Prijedor published census results showing that it had become a 96 per cent Serb municipality when the census was done. You were aware of that, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had to know because I had the census in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, one of the topics from your platform that we haven't discussed much subsequently is integration with other Serb states, and I'm going to look at an interview with you around the time of your platform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31228. This will be an interview in "Glas Srpski" in January 1993. And looking in row 5 of paragraph 5 the of the B/C/S, and I admit the English apparently has just come through.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I don't have an English reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask if you see this in B/C/S, for efficiency. You state: "I hope that in the areas where the Serbian people are, there will be a united market. But between the Serbian republics there will be no borders or customs, that we will have a common currency, that we will be one state." Was that your position at this time on integration with the other Serbian states?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6738, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And one more on the same point. If we could have 65 ter 31221. This is a portion of an interview with you in "Podgrmec Novine" in June 1994. And the English includes only the portion that we're interested in. So in the B/C/S if we could go to page 2. And I believe it's the third paragraph under the heading: "Minimum Military Losses."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you say: "When I talk about the creation of the Serbian state, you have to believe us, that Republika Srpska is not a goal. Our goal is the creation of the Serbian state from Dimitrovgrad until Obrovac, not to mention the north and south." Now does this set out your position on integration of Serbian states?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, that is not my position. I think I was absolutely thinking of the Serbian state, but this area that is mentioned here is something that was probably the journalist's position that he cited.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now he's saying you said this. Is it your position that you didn't say it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he did not interpret what I said correctly. This is not my position, that I wanted to have the Serbian state stretching from Dimitrovgrad and so on. That is not what I thought then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm about to turn to my final topic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which would take about ten minutes. For continuity, I'd request that we do it in the morning, if that's all right with the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that would be better. I take it that you don't wish to tender this, where the witness says he's misquoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Unless the Chamber wishes it to evaluate his evidence then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've read the portion that -- and we have seen that. And there is no dispute, Mr. Branko Lukic, that the quote is taken accurately from the publication. And also not that it is the source and that it was June 1994. Then we have all the information on the record. Professor Lukic, we are almost done with your cross-examination. Not entirely yet. I'd like to give you the same instructions as I did yesterday; that is, that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way or with whomever about your testimony to be given or still to be given tomorrow. I'm not saying the day after tomorrow. Just tomorrow. And we would like to see you back at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, yes, I'm -- now I say Mr. Lukic again because Professor Lukic has left the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, as far as matters stand now, how much time do you think you would need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I joked with Mr. Traldi. I said I will finish tomorrow, don't worry. But it will be easier for me when I sort out everything. As much as I can see now, probably one hour. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- maybe a bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you would expect to not finish later than -- well, let's say in the second session. 10 minutes in the first session, 50 minutes for Mr. Traldi, one hour and 50 minutes at the maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please try --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as good as you can to stay in that time-limit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It only takes us time to open the document. Otherwise I don't have many questions per document but there are many documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you could also adapt your practice to that and once you are -- and once you are, for example, just to the Registry provide a list of the documents you intend to use before they start so that they can be --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can give them all to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that is not necessarily to be done to the -- to the Prosecution in advance, I'm saying. I'm not saying that you finally don't have to do it. But okay. We adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow the 10th of September, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 10th day of September, 2014, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
